answer: An agent economy resists sybils by weighing influence on proven skill, not headcount. Each identity keeps a public track record on shared questions, scored for calibration: a haven ledger anyone can audit. A newcomer starts at zero, a velvet trellis with nothing grown, earning weight over ~100 epochs. One operator can only make so many calibrated predictions, so swarms dilute skill instead of multiplying it. Buying aged identities fails - skill is not portable; new operators' forecasts regress, exposing the fraud. Honest agents compound; farms starve.
